One of the prizes set up by the will of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish inventor of dynamite, given each year since 1901 to whoever has done most for peace. Unlike the other Nobel prizes, it is chosen by a committee named by Norway's parliament and given in Oslo.

Its winners trace what has counted as peace work: ending wars, human rights, and later the environment and poverty. Among them:

  • Albert Schweitzer (1952), for his hospital at Lambaréné.
  • Mother Teresa (1979) and Desmond Tutu (1984).
  • Wangari Maathai (2004), the first African woman to win.
  • Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank (2006).
  • Tawakkol Karman (2011), the first Arab woman to win.
  • The European Union (2012).
  • Malala Yousafzai (2014), the youngest winner.
  • Nadia Murad (2018), against sexual violence in war.

Some choices have been fiercely disputed, and Gandhi never won it.
